input: Under COLREGs Rule 5, every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by which of the following?
choices: Radar observation, but only when visibility is restricted
Sight and hearing as well as all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances
Sight alone, with radar and AIS as optional supplements
Continuous AIS and radar monitoring, which together satisfy the look-out requirement

input: Under COLREGs Rule 7, if there is any doubt as to whether risk of collision exists with an approaching vessel, what shall be assumed?
choices: Risk does not exist until confirmed by radar plotting
Risk exists only if the other vessel is within 3 nautical miles
Such risk shall be deemed to exist
The give-way vessel will resolve the doubt by manoeuvring first

input: Two power-driven vessels are meeting on reciprocal courses so as to involve risk of collision (a head-on situation). Under COLREGs Rule 14, what action is required?
choices: Each vessel shall alter her course to starboard so that each passes on the port side of the other
The faster vessel shall alter course while the slower vessel stands on
Each vessel shall alter her course to port so that each passes on the starboard side of the other
Both vessels shall stop engines and communicate by VHF before manoeuvring

input: Two power-driven vessels are crossing so as to involve risk of collision. Under COLREGs Rule 15, which vessel shall keep out of the way?
choices: The vessel which is to windward of the other
The vessel which has the other on her own port side
The smaller of the two vessels
The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side

input: Under UNCLOS Article 17, which ships enjoy the right of innocent passage through the territorial sea?
choices: Ships of all States, whether coastal or land-locked
Only ships of States that share a maritime boundary with the coastal State
Only merchant ships, with government ships excluded
Only ships that have obtained prior authorisation from the coastal State

input: Under UNCLOS Article 18, passage through the territorial sea must be continuous and expeditious. In which of the following circumstances may a ship nevertheless stop and anchor?
choices: Whenever the master considers it commercially convenient
When stopping is incidental to ordinary navigation, or rendered necessary by force majeure or distress, or to render assistance to persons, ships or aircraft in danger
Only after receiving express clearance from the coastal State's port authority
Whenever the ship remains more than 3 nautical miles from the coast

input: Under UNCLOS Article 20, how are submarines required to navigate when exercising innocent passage in the territorial sea?
choices: Submerged, provided they proceed at a safe speed
At periscope depth, provided they broadcast their position on AIS
On the surface, but only inside designated sea lanes
On the surface and showing their flag

input: Which State bears the primary responsibility for ensuring that a merchant ship on the high seas complies with international safety, manning and pollution standards?
choices: The State in whose waters the ship was last inspected
The State of the ship's beneficial owner
The flag State whose flag the ship is entitled to fly
The nearest coastal State at the time of the voyage

input: A foreign-flagged cargo ship is voluntarily in port when inspectors find deficiencies that are clearly hazardous to safety. Under port State control, what may the port State do?
choices: Nothing beyond reporting the deficiencies to the flag State
Inspect the ship and detain her until the deficiencies that are clearly hazardous are rectified
Prosecute the crew under the flag State's national law
Revoke the ship's registration and certificates

input: In which maritime zone does the coastal State exercise full sovereignty, subject to the right of innocent passage for foreign ships?
choices: The exclusive economic zone
The contiguous zone
The high seas
The territorial sea
